items.headline: Workers' Party calls special conference on Pritam Singh's future after court upholds conviction
items.summary: The Workers' Party has called a special cadres conference for 28 June to decide secretary-general Pritam Singh's future, after the High Court upheld his conviction for lying to Parliament's Committee of Privileges; 25 cadres requisitioned the meeting, and Singh faces a secret ballot if he declines to step down.

items.headline: Singapore to ease hotel restrictions at Boat Quay and Beach Road heritage precincts
items.summary: National Development Minister Chee Hong Tat said curbs on new hotels, backpackers' hostels and serviced apartments will be relaxed at the Boat Quay and Beach Road heritage precincts to help rejuvenate the areas while conserving their character.

items.headline: Another Singaporean arrested in Malaysia over Cambodia-based scam syndicate
items.summary: Police said another Singaporean man was arrested in Malaysia for his suspected role in a Cambodia-based scam syndicate that targeted victims in Singapore, the latest cross-border arrest in a widening crackdown on the networks behind the city-state's scam losses.

items.headline: Singapore to screen 2026 World Cup matches free at community venues
items.summary: Selected 2026 FIFA World Cup matches will be screened free of charge at 52 community clubs, five ActiveSG sports centres and The Kallang, giving residents public venues to watch the tournament.

items.headline: India designates Surha Tal in Uttar Pradesh as its 100th Ramsar wetland site
items.summary: India crossed 100 wetlands of international importance with the addition of Surha Tal, the Jai Prakash Narayan Bird Sanctuary in Ballia, Uttar Pradesh; Prime Minister Narendra Modi hailed the milestone, noting 67 sites have been added since 2014.

items.headline: Oil India reports second Andaman offshore gas discovery
items.summary: Oil India said it struck natural gas at its Vijayapuram-3 exploratory well off the Andaman Islands, about 15km offshore in 355m of water, the second find in its three-well Andaman campaign after Vijayapuram-2; Petroleum Minister Hardeep Singh Puri announced the discovery.

items.headline: Indian rupee hovers near record low against the dollar as markets stay cautious
items.summary: The rupee traded near a record low of about 95.6 to the US dollar on Friday, pressured by elevated crude prices and foreign outflows, while the Sensex and Nifty edged up around 0.2 per cent.

items.headline: India hosts 11th BRICS foreign-policy planning dialogue in New Delhi
items.summary: India hosted the 11th BRICS Foreign Policy Planning Dialogue in New Delhi, with policy-planning chiefs from member states discussing global forecasting, resilience and cooperation amid a volatile geopolitical climate.

items.headline: Russia and Ukraine trade large overnight strikes; Kyiv hits St Petersburg
items.summary: Russia fired more than 400 drones and over 40 missiles at Ukrainian cities overnight, killing at least seven people including first responders, Ukrainian officials said; hours later Ukraine struck targets near St Petersburg after President Zelensky ordered the operation and Vladimir Putin rejected his offer of direct talks.

items.headline: Peru holds presidential election this weekend in a polarized, tight race
items.summary: Peruvians vote this weekend to choose a new president in a polarized contest that opinion polls suggest is too close to call, the latest test of stability in a country that has churned through leaders in recent years.

items.headline: Suno raises $400 million at a $5.4 billion valuation despite copyright lawsuits
items.summary: AI music startup Suno raised a $400 million Series D led by Bond, more than doubling its valuation to $5.4 billion in about seven months, even as Universal, Sony and other rights holders pursue copyright suits; the company says it has passed 2 million subscribers.

items.headline: Coralogix raises $200 million to monitor AI agents
items.summary: Observability startup Coralogix raised $200 million, betting that the spread of autonomous AI agents will drive demand for tools to monitor, troubleshoot and manage increasingly independent software systems.

items.headline: Update: Apple's WWDC opens Monday with its biggest Siri overhaul in years
items.summary: Apple opens WWDC on 8 June with a long-delayed Siri revamp set to headline; reporting points to a standalone Siri app, a ChatGPT-style conversational mode, agentic actions across apps and an in-house web-search engine to power answers, alongside iOS 27.

items.headline: Wall Street's chip stocks tumble, wiping over $1 trillion in value
items.summary: The Nasdaq fell about 4 per cent on Friday, its worst day since April 2025, and the S&P 500 dropped 2.6 per cent as a rout in chip stocks erased more than $1 trillion in market value; Nvidia fell around 6 per cent after Broadcom's cautious AI outlook and a strong May jobs report lifted bond yields.

items.headline: Amazon unveils new warehouse robot as Big Tech AI layoffs continue
items.summary: Amazon showed off its latest warehouse robot, with robotics chief Tye Brady arguing that automation is creating jobs, even as major technology firms including Meta cut staff amid a multibillion-dollar push into artificial intelligence.

items.headline: SpaceX sets fixed $135-a-share price in $75 billion IPO
items.summary: SpaceX plans to sell about 555.6 million shares at a fixed $135 each to raise roughly $75 billion in its initial public offering, an unusual structure that skips traditional book-building; the roadshow is set to begin around 8 June ahead of a planned Nasdaq listing.

items.headline: Update: Andreeva wins French Open for her first Grand Slam title
items.summary: Mirra Andreeva, 19, beat Polish qualifier Maja Chwalinska 6-3, 6-2 in Saturday's Roland Garros final to claim her maiden Grand Slam title, becoming the youngest woman to win in Paris since Monica Seles in 1992.

items.headline: Update: Antonelli takes maiden Monaco pole as Leclerc crashes
items.summary: Kimi Antonelli claimed his first Monaco pole with a 1:12.051, edging Max Verstappen by 0.043s, with Lewis Hamilton third; home favourite Charles Leclerc crashed at Tabac on his final lap and will start Sunday's race fourth.

items.headline: Update: England close on Lord's win as Robinson rips through New Zealand
items.summary: Ollie Robinson's double strike left New Zealand 55-5, chasing 254, on a rain-shortened third day of the first Test at Lord's, where only 9.4 overs were possible; Robinson holds match figures of 7-57 as England closed in on victory.

fun_fact.headline: The University of Oxford is older than the Aztec Empire
fun_fact.body: Teaching at the University of Oxford dates back to at least 1096, and it had grown into a recognisable university by the early 1200s. The Aztec Empire, by contrast, was founded only in 1428, with its capital Tenochtitlan established in 1325 - so Oxford was already centuries old before the Aztec Empire came into being.

puzzle.title: The Sealed Room
puzzle.body: A man comes home, opens the door, and finds Antonio and Maria lying dead on the floor of a sealed room. Around them is a pool of water and some broken glass. There are no wounds on the bodies, and nobody else has entered the room. What happened?
puzzle.approach: Question your assumptions about who - or what - Antonio and Maria are.
puzzle.answer: Antonio and Maria are fish. Something - a gust of wind, a pet, or a knock - toppled their glass bowl. The bowl shattered, the water spilled out, and without it the fish died. The phrase 'sealed room' is a red herring: no human intruder was ever involved.
